doc.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025

title: Enriching the Kentucky community
summary: He has not been outplayed by students; his greatest achievement is enriching Lexington through high school bands, a duo and former students.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I’m going to leapfrog to after you’ve had these students for years perhaps —
Okay. Have you ever had students who get to the point who can play things that you can’t?

Not really, and that’s because I mean I don’t expect all my colleagues to do what I’ve done, which is my own passion for playing. I mean I — people would say to me, “Why are you in Kentucky?” I’d say, “Well why are you anywhere?” I said because you can be an asset to that community. When I stepped foot in Kentucky and started that it was a one-year appointment. And I knew after the first month that I didn’t want to leave because there was activity in the trumpet there but it was not anything extraordinary. And so now I think the thing I feel the best about, besides the students that are teaching at other universities and playing in service bands and professional groups and things, other orchestras, I think my greatest achievement is having enriched the community in which I live. What could be better? You know I found out my neighbor, he plays all over the world. You know after you’ve lived there for twenty years. Because he’d never played there. You know he’d go out on these trips and traveling, and then you play one recital a year at the university you know and that’s it. And then nobody comes to that most of the time except other faculty and friends. So basically like I started a duo there because when I got there there was nothing for me to play in in Kentucky. It was 110,000 people in Lexington and now there’s almost 400,000. So I said well I’ve got to do something here so I’m going to volunteer to play with high school bands. I just visited in Florida here with the band director of the first concert I did with a high school band in Kentucky. Excellent band. And he asked me, and his son played trumpet. So I gave his son trumpet lessons and you know I played with him at the Midwest Band Clinic. I played with all the best bands in Kentucky at the Midwest Band Clinic. And to me that was the greatest thing. And today I have students all over not only of course other places but Kentucky,

that teach in schools, that are excellent teachers. I have students that teach other young people about trumpet. I have students — all the students in my big band they were students at U.K. See? And they wouldn’t be in there if they couldn’t play it. Because they know me better, and it’s like my son, right? You know he’s a great trumpet player. He taught at — I think it was Colgate, I’m not sure.
